summary: The Youth Coding Workshop program, begun September 5, 2023 and led by Julian Torres and Maria Gomez, teaches programming to students aged 10 to 18 through free workshops in schools, libraries, and community centers. It stresses inclusivity, collaboration, soft skills, and ethics, supported by local tech companies and schools. Founders plan to expand to rural areas and online, and success is measured by both quantitative and qualitative outcomes.
one_line: A free local youth coding workshop program, launched in 2023, teaches programming and soft skills to ages 10-18 and aims to expand.
key_facts: The Youth Coding Workshop program began on September 5, 2023.
The program is led by software engineer Julian Torres and educator Maria Gomez.
Workshops teach Python, Java, and Scratch to students aged 10 to 18.
Each workshop series has 10 weekly sessions, with 2 hours of hands-on learning per session.
The workshops are free, with scholarships for materials and equipment provided to those who need it.
Julian Torres said, "It's essential that we break down the barriers to entry in tech for underrepresented groups."
The program is sponsored by large tech companies and small start-ups, providing resources, mentorship, and guest speakers.
Teachers at partner schools can recommend students who show aptitude or interest in technology.
Sarah Chen, a 14-year-old participant, said the workshops made her believe in herself.
A typical workshop day includes a brief lecture, Q&A, team projects, and a showcase for feedback.
The curriculum is periodically updated to include artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain, and teaches ethics such as privacy and security.
Founders plan additional sites and online platforms to reach rural and remote communities, and a learning pathway through college and tech careers.
Workshops host family coding nights and community hackathons to engage parents and the community.

Success is measured by lines of code written and students advancing to advanced courses, as well as joy of learning and community spirit; some former participants have won coding competitions or landed internships.
